analysis:
Examined docs/architecture/inference.md. The supplied head excerpts cover lines 4931-5450, which are unchanged context. The actual PR change is a new section at head lines 4816-4826 (GPT-OSS decode command buffers), plus a date bump on line 3, and that section is not in the supplied text units. The patch_excerpt shows it only describes decode committing a Metal command buffer every 100 operations with no input-size bound via GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers, claiming results do not depend on partitioning and prefill keeps MLX defaults. This is documentation only. It adds no code, wire change, key handling, attestation change or authorization change, so I found no regression against TB-002, TB-007, T-041 or A-001. The surrounding Qwen media, TP and prefix-cache text is pre-existing and is not restated as new. I did not re-verify its claims.

The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer moved from 7933a0fa to 63baac23. The supplied evidence contains only the pointer bump, with no diff of the submodule contents. I therefore cannot assess what changed in the inference engine. That could include the GPT-OSS command-buffer limit code (CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding), the KV or prefix cache, memory handling, or decrypted-prompt lifetime in TB-007 and T-028. Coverage limit: the submodule diff is unreviewed, so the security conclusion for that unit is uncertain. A reviewer with access to the submodule diff should check for changes to prompt-data retention, cache scoping, and resource-exhaustion behavior under the unbounded input-size command buffers (a GPU memory or availability concern, T-029). The doc's claim that results are partition-independent is unverified. No finding is raised from missing evidence.
